title: Mean of a sum of two random variables
stem: \(X\) has mean \({a|int}\) and variance 4. \(Y\) is independent of \(X\) and has mean \({c|int}\) and variance 2. Find \(\operatorname{E}(X+Y)\).

steps.name: A
steps.note: A is a+c. Original means 5 and 3 give 8.

title: Variance of a sum of independent random variables
source: Theory S2-3.2 Quick check 2 (6); Var(X+Y)=Var(X)+Var(Y) when independent
stem: \(X\) has variance \({b|int}\) and \(Y\) is independent of \(X\) with variance \({d|int}\). Find \(\operatorname{Var}(X+Y)\).

steps.name: A
steps.note: A is b+d. Original variances 4 and 2 give 6.

title: Variance of a linear combination of independent random variables
source: Theory S2-3.2 Quick check 3 (18); Var(2X-Y)=4 Var(X)+Var(Y)
stem: \(X\) has variance \({b|int}\) and \(Y\) is independent of \(X\) with variance \({d|int}\). Find \(\operatorname{Var}(2X-Y)\).

steps.name: A
steps.note: A is 4b+d. Original variances 4 and 2 give 18.

title: Mean and variance of the sum of four independent values

source.note: 9709/73/O/N/19 Question 1(i) only [2], with the official opening sentence. Official QP and official MS. Part (ii) omitted (already used in S2-3.1).

stem:
This question is 9709/73/O/N/19 Question 1(i) only, taken from the official QP. The official opening sentence is included so that the part is self-contained.

The random variable X has mean 2.4 and variance 3.1.

(i) The random variable Y is the sum of four independent values of X. Find the mean and variance of Y. [2]

steps.name: C
steps.note: Official MS: B1, 12.4. Independent: 4 times 3.1 = 12.4, because the four values are independent.

contexts.note: Stem taken from the official QP PDF, Question 1(i) only, with the official opening. Official MS reproduced mark by mark. Paper/self-mark.
